feedback: If a learner selects a constraint-breaker, point out that a failed must-meet gate eliminates an option regardless of how well it scores on other rows.
If a justification cites preference rather than rows, require it to name the specific criteria the chosen solution wins and the trade-off it accepts.
activities.intendedInsight: Drawing the right conclusion from a comparison means reading across shared criteria, gating constraint-breakers first, and tying the choice to named rows.
learnerActions: Given a completed solutions×criteria matrix, choose the most promising solution and state why in terms of the rows.
Sort candidate options into 'meets constraints' and 'eliminated' categories.
Rank the solutions that remain after setting aside any that fail a must-meet constraint by overall fit against the criteria.
Complete a 'chosen because…' justification that references specific rows of the matrix.
activities.title: Judge pre-filled comparisons
